newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa trade bases hopes on eastern Europe.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa trade bases hopes on eastern Europe.

text.p: Growth in demand for chocolate products in eastern Europe should secure future markets for Germany's cocoa trade, the VRBF trade organisation said.
Germany's high per-capita chocolate consumption and expanding markets in eastern Europe guarantee favourable future business prospects, it said in its annual report.
In 1996, Germany processed 17 percent of global cocoa crops.

In a statement last Friday export promoters "German Sweets" showed central and eastern European countries accounted for 200,000 tonnes of total exports of 306,000 tonnes in 1996 (263,000 tonnes in 1995).

But VRBF, which represents 34 importers, exporters and brokers, said while implied raw materials consumption was rising in Germany a change in trade flows meant relatively more beans and semis were processed in western Europe and at origin. The trade was confident it could change itrs role towards becoming a provider of increasingly sophisticated ingredients for confectionery manufacture.

Of 294,099 tonnes of beans imported in 1996 (up 3.4 percent from 1995), 60.1 percent came from Ivory Coast, up from 57.2 percent a year earlier, the annual report also showed. Imports from Ghana rose to 17.6 percent from 14.1.

VRBF noted German imports from Malaysia fell drastically to 1,579 tonnes in 1996 from 8,241 tonnes in 1995 and versus nearly 50,000 tonnes in the early 1990s. Malaysia now processes more than 80 percent of its cocoa at home.

South East Asian suppliers accounted for just 12 percent of bean imports into Germany in 1996 after 16 percent in 1995. West Africa's share was nearly 85 percent from 59. --Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
